subject: Chemistry
scope: Mock-eligible short recall of AQA rate equations, RP7 data interpretation and Kp (taught A-level topics only)
notes: Eleven concise conceptual/reasoning checks; supplements existing core and mock recall, without claims of full specification coverage.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In an initial-rate clock experiment, when can 1/t be used as a measure proportional to initial rate?
cards.back: When every trial uses the same small, fixed reaction extent and conditions are comparable.
accept: When every trial uses the same small, fixed reaction extent and conditions are comparable.
The same fixed small amount of reaction occurs in each trial.
Each trial reaches the same fixed small amount of product.
A fixed small threshold of reaction is reached in each trial.
reject: 1/t is always the exact rate constant.
Only if temperature varies between runs.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: On a reactant concentration–time graph, what does the tangent gradient at one time measure?
cards.back: The instantaneous rate of change of reactant concentration, d[A]/dt (negative for a disappearing reactant).
accept: The instantaneous rate of change of reactant concentration, d[A]/dt (negative for a disappearing reactant).
The instantaneous rate of change of concentration.
reject: The average rate over the entire reaction.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: For disappearance of reactant A, how do you obtain a positive rate from d[A]/dt?
accept: Multiply the reactant concentration gradient by −1.
reject: Rate = d[A]/dt, which must always be positive.
Use the area under the graph.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What shape does [A] against time have for a zero-order reaction while reactant remains?
cards.back: A straight line with constant negative gradient, −k.
accept: A straight line with constant negative gradient, −k.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to the half-life of a first-order reaction at constant temperature as concentration falls?
accept: The half-life is independent of concentration.
reject: It doubles every time concentration halves.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: If rate = k[A]²[B] and [A] doubles at constant [B] and temperature, what happens to the rate?
cards.back: It becomes four times as large.
accept: It becomes four times as large.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the gradient of a graph of ln k against 1/T for the Arrhenius relationship?
accept: Negative activation energy divided by the gas constant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the vertical intercept of an Arrhenius graph of ln k against 1/T?
cards.back: ln A, where A is the Arrhenius constant.
accept: ln A, where A is the Arrhenius constant.
Natural logarithm of the Arrhenius constant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is the partial pressure of gas i calculated from its mole fraction and the total pressure?
accept: Partial pressure equals mole fraction times total pressure.
reject: Mole fraction divided by total pressure.
Multiply the number of moles by temperature.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: If total pressure changes but temperature remains constant, what happens to the value of Kp?
cards.back: Kp is unchanged; only temperature alters its value.
accept: Kp is unchanged; only temperature alters its value.
No change in Kp at constant temperature.
